What I hate on Linux is it's USB mass storage support. You need to also invoke "sync" to make sure that all the buffers are flushed to the actual filesystem, or, even better, properly unmount it, which includes flushing the buffers, too.

EDIT: To be more precise, this is really a performance optimization rather than a flaw. The kernel just keeps all the data to be written in buffers in the very fast memory and does the slower write operations with a delay. I think that it is the case in any OS, though, which is why you are always warned about just unplugging a drive without actually unmounting it.
